title: Implicit elimination of unit-twisted formal monoid variables
statement:
Let $(D,\mathfrak n)$ be a nonzero complete Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $S,T$ be fine saturated monoids [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] which are sharp, meaning that $0$ is the only invertible element of each. Let $ eta:S	o T$ be a homomorphism with $ eta^{-1}(0)=\{0\}$. For such a sharp monoid $P$, write $D[[P]]$ for the completion of the monoid ring $D[P]$, with basis $[p]$ and multiplication $[p][p']=[p+p']$, at $(\mathfrak n,[p]:p
e0)$. Put $H=D[[S\oplus T]]$, and denote its $S$- and $T$-monomials by $X^s$ and $Y^t$. Let $u:S	o D[[S]]^	imes$ be a homomorphism to the multiplicative group of units. Let $I$ be the ideal of $H$ generated by $X^s-u(s)Y^{ eta(s)}$ for $s\in S$. The map $D[[T]]	o H/I$ induced by coefficients and $Y$-monomials is a continuous isomorphism. Its inverse sends every $X^s$ with $s
e0$ into the ideal $(Y^t:t
e0)$, and induces the identity on $D$ after killing all nonzero $T$-monomials.

source.place: ILO VI 2.3, printed p.73, formal Kummer chart formula: auxiliary implicit substitution needed to retain arbitrary chart unit twists; agent-supplied algebraic detail.

proof.text: Put $A=D[[T]]$, $\mathfrak m_A=(\mathfrak n,Y^t:t\ne0)$, and $\mathfrak m_H=(\mathfrak n,X^s,Y^t:s,t\ne0)$. Finite generation of $S,T$ gives surjections from finite-variable polynomial $D$-algebras onto $D[S],D[T],D[S\oplus T]$: send one variable to each chosen monoid generator. Thus these algebras are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Their displayed defining ideals are finitely generated. Their completions, including $A,H$, are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], and complete and separated for the extended defining ideals by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal]. The same node identifies their residue quotients with $D/\mathfrak n$, a nonzero field.

source.place: ILO VI 2.3, printed p.73, displayed completed Kummer chart formulas; agent-supplied implicit elimination retaining unit twists

proof.text: These defining ideals are the maximal ideals of the completed rings. Indeed, if $f$ has nonzero residue in $D/\mathfrak n$, choose $d\in D^\times$ with the same residue and write $f=d(1-v)$ with $v$ in the defining ideal. The partial sums $1+v+\cdots+v^N$ have compatible residues modulo every power, and their limit is inverse to $1-v$. Thus every element outside the defining ideal is invertible, while an element inside cannot be invertible because the residue field is nonzero. In particular $A,H$ are nonzero complete Noetherian local rings.

source.place: ILO VI 2.3, printed p.73, displayed completed Kummer chart formulas; agent-supplied implicit elimination retaining unit twists

proof.text: Choose nonzero generators $s_1,\ldots,s_h$ of $S$. For a monoid homomorphism $a:S\to(A,\cdot)$ taking nonzero elements into $\mathfrak m_A$, let $E_a:D[[S]]\to A$ be [lem-per-formal-monoid-adic-evaluation] with coefficient inclusion. Define $F(a)(s)=E_a(u(s))Y^{\beta(s)}$. Both factors are multiplicative in $s$, and $F(a)(0)=1$. Since $\beta(s)\ne0$ for $s\ne0$, $F(a)(s)\in\mathfrak m_A$. If $a(s_i)-b(s_i)\in\mathfrak m_A^r$, the congruence clause of the cited node gives $E_a(u(s))-E_b(u(s))\in\mathfrak m_A^r$ for every $s$. Consequently $F(a)(s)-F(b)(s)\in\mathfrak m_A^{r+1}$ for every nonzero $s$. This contraction preserves every relation of $S$ because its arguments and outputs are monoid homomorphisms.

source.place: ILO VI 2.3, printed p.73, displayed completed Kummer chart formulas; agent-supplied implicit elimination retaining unit twists

proof.text: Set $a_0(0)=1$ and $a_0(s)=0$ for $s\ne0$. This is multiplicative: sharpness implies that $s+s'=0$ only when $s=s'=0$. Define $a_{k+1}=F(a_k)$. First $a_1(s)-a_0(s)\in\mathfrak m_A$ for every nonzero $s$. Induction using the contraction gives $a_{k+1}(s)-a_k(s)\in\mathfrak m_A^{k+1}$. For each $s$, its residues modulo $\mathfrak m_A^r$ therefore stabilize as $k\to\infty$. Completeness gives a unique element $a(s)$ with these stabilized residues. The identities $a_k(0)=1$ and $a_k(s+s')=a_k(s)a_k(s')$ hold modulo every power at the limit, so separatedness gives $a(0)=1$ and $a(s+s')=a(s)a(s')$. Also $a(s)\in\mathfrak m_A$ for $s\ne0$.

source.place: ILO VI 2.3, printed p.73, displayed completed Kummer chart formulas; agent-supplied implicit elimination retaining unit twists

proof.text: For every $r\ge1$, the construction gives $a(s_i)-a_k(s_i)\in\mathfrak m_A^r$ whenever $k\ge r$. The congruence clause of [lem-per-formal-monoid-adic-evaluation] shows that $E_a(u(s))-E_{a_k}(u(s))\in\mathfrak m_A^r$. Passing to stabilized residues in $a_{k+1}(s)=E_{a_k}(u(s))Y^{\beta(s)}$, and using separatedness, yields the exact fixed-point equations $a(s)=E_a(u(s))Y^{\beta(s)}$ for every $s$. In particular every nonzero $a(s)$ (with $s\ne0$) is a multiple of the individual monomial $Y^{\beta(s)}$; no closedness assertion about the monomial ideal is needed.

source.place: ILO VI 2.3, printed p.73, displayed completed Kummer chart formulas; agent-supplied implicit elimination retaining unit twists

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-formal-monoid-adic-evaluation] to $S\oplus T$ and the monoid homomorphism $(s,t)\mapsto a(s)Y^t$. It gives a continuous $D$-algebra map $\phi:H\to A$ fixing every $Y^t$. Its restriction to $D[[S]]$ is $E_a$ by uniqueness of evaluation. The fixed-point equations imply $\phi(X^s-u(s)Y^{\beta(s)})=0$, hence $I\subseteq\ker\phi$. Since $\phi(1)=1$ and $A\ne0$, $I$ is proper. There is an induced continuous map $\bar\phi:C=H/I\to A$ for the quotient topology.

source.place: ILO VI 2.3, printed p.73, displayed completed Kummer chart formulas; agent-supplied implicit elimination retaining unit twists

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient], $C$ is a Noetherian complete local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_C=\mathfrak m_H/I$. Apply [lem-per-formal-monoid-adic-evaluation] to $T$, with target $C$ and $t\mapsto\overline{Y^t}$, to obtain the continuous coefficient-and-monomial map $j:A\to C$ in the statement. The quotient topology on $C$ is precisely its maximal-ideal-adic topology since the images of $\mathfrak m_H^r$ are $\mathfrak m_C^r$. The composite $\bar\phi j$ fixes $D$ and all $Y^t$, so uniqueness of evaluation gives $\bar\phi j=\operatorname{id}_A$.

source.place: ILO VI 2.3, printed p.73, displayed completed Kummer chart formulas; agent-supplied implicit elimination retaining unit twists

proof.text: In $C$, put $b(s)=\overline{X^s}$ and $c(s)=j(a(s))$. These are monoid homomorphisms sending nonzero elements to $\mathfrak m_C$. Evaluation uniqueness shows that evaluation at $b$ is the quotient map restricted to $D[[S]]$, and evaluation at $c$ is $jE_a$. Thus the defining relations and Step 5 give $b(s)=E_b(u(s))\overline{Y^{\beta(s)}}$ and $c(s)=E_c(u(s))\overline{Y^{\beta(s)}}$. Initially $b(s)-c(s)\in\mathfrak m_C$. If the generator differences lie in $\mathfrak m_C^r$, the congruence clause of [lem-per-formal-monoid-adic-evaluation], followed by multiplication by $\overline{Y^{\beta(s)}}\in\mathfrak m_C$, places all differences in $\mathfrak m_C^{r+1}$. Induction and separatedness give $b(s)=c(s)$ for every $s$.

source.place: ILO VI 2.3, printed p.73, displayed completed Kummer chart formulas; agent-supplied implicit elimination retaining unit twists

proof.text: Let $q:H\to C$ be the quotient map. The continuous maps $q$ and $j\bar\phi q$ agree on $D$, all $X^s$ by Step 8, and all $Y^t$ by construction. Uniqueness in [lem-per-formal-monoid-adic-evaluation], now for $S\oplus T$, gives $q=j\bar\phi q$. Surjectivity of $q$ gives $j\bar\phi=\operatorname{id}_C$. Together with Step 7 this proves that $j$ is a continuous isomorphism with continuous inverse $\bar\phi$.

source.place: ILO VI 2.3, printed p.73, displayed completed Kummer chart formulas; agent-supplied implicit elimination retaining unit twists

proof.text:
For $s
e0$, the inverse sends $\overline{X^s}$ to $a(s)=E_a(u(s))Y^{ eta(s)}\in(Y^t:t
e0)A$, since $ eta(s)
e0$. It fixes every coefficient $d\in D$. Reducing modulo the nonzero $T$-monomials therefore leaves $d$ unchanged and kills each nonzero $X$-monomial. Equivalently, compose with the continuous augmentation $A	o D$, given by evaluation at $Y^0=1$ and $Y^t=0$ for $t
e0$; the evaluation node applies because $D$ is $\mathfrak n$-adically complete. This composite is the identity on $D$, as required.
